correctness.rationale: With high=degree>2, low=degree≤2 in finite simple acyclic undirected labeled graphs, a planted low root has at most one child and any planted high root has at least two low children: L=x(1+L+H), H=x(e^L−1−L). Root an actual vertex to get T•=x(1+P+P²/2)+x(e^L−1−L−L²/2), P=L+H. Undirected-edge-rooted EGF L²/2+LH; oriented-edge-rooted EGF L²+2LH. The standard dissymmetry identity yields U=T•−L²/2−LH, all labeled forests F=e^U. This formal-power-series proof covers arbitrary finite orders, no convergence assumption. Independent exact rational expansions recovered all connected/forest coefficients n≤12 and Prüfer-code exhaustive connected counts n≤7.
